newsitem.title: UK: SmithKline says 5 major drugs in Phase III.
newsitem.headline: SmithKline says 5 major drugs in Phase III.

text.p: British based pharmaceutical group SmithKline Beecham Plc said on Tuesday it had five new drugs in Phase III development, all of which had great potential.

Chief executive Jan Leschly told a post results news conference that the five, which all went into late stage trials in 1996, would be successful if they could generate annual sales of between 300 million and 500 million stg.
"Each of them we believe have big potential for the future," Leschly said, adding "if we could get 300 to 500 million in sales from each of these we'll be doing all right."
Leschly, who said the group's 1996 sales were driven by a strong rise in sales of new pharmaceuticals, highlighted compound SB207266, a development intented to treat irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).
"If we could find a drug for that it is going to be a big drug," he said.

Also on the list are Memric, a partial agonist for Alzheimer's Disease, Keliximab, a new treatment for rheumatoid arthritis, asthma and psoriasis, BRL49653, an insulin sensitizer for type-2 diabetes and a new type of migraine drug codenamed SB220453.
Leschly said sales of new products, defined as drugs introduced in the past five years, rose 37 percent last year to to 1.54 billion stg, representing 36 percent of SmithKline Beecham's total sales.
"This is a clear indication of innnovation - of productive research and development," Leschly said.
